Item 2.02. Results of Operations and Financial Condition. The information appearing below under Item 4.02(a) regarding certain previously reported financial information of GoPro, Inc. (the “Company”) for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 and the fiscal quarter and year-to-date periods ended September 30, 2025, March 31, 2026, and June 30, 2026 is incorporated herein by reference into this Item 2.02. The information appearing below under Item 4.02(a) refers to certain financial statements that the Company intends to restate. The Company identified certain errors related to accounting for certain debt instruments. The errors related to (i) the initial measurement of the liability classified warrants issued to Mateo Financing, LLC (the “Warrants”) on August 4, 2025, (ii) recognition of changes in fair value of the warrant liability at each subsequent reporting period, (iii) the accounting for the November 5, 2025 Warrant repricing in connection with an amendment to the 2025 Credit Agreement, and (iv) debt discount amortization due to initial measurement errors. A separate error was identified related to the accounting for the Company's convertible debentures (the "Convertible Debentures") issued in 2026 as part of the Securities Purchase Agreement entered into with YA II PN, Ltd. In accounting for the bifurcation of the embedded conversion derivative from the Convertible Debentures, the Company used the fair value of the convertible debenture as the fair value of the embedded conversion derivative, rather than determining the fair value of the embedded conversion derivative using a with-and-without valuation approach and recognizing the combined instrument as short-term debt. As a result, the amounts initially allocated to the embedded conversion derivative and debt host at issuance, and the related debt discount and subsequent interest expense, were incorrectly recorded. These errors do not affect the Company's revenue, gross margin, operating loss, cash, operating cash flows, EBITDA or non-GAAP operating income (loss) in any of the restated periods. However, the corrections affect net loss and other non-cash adjustments within the adjustments to reconcile net loss to net cash used in operating activities, with offsetting adjustments such that net cash used in operating activities remains unchanged. Item 4.02. Non-Reliance on Previously Issued Financial Statements or a Related Audit Report or Completed Interim Review. (a) While preparing the proxy statement related to the transactions contemplated by the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of September 1, 2026, by and among the Company, Action Acquisitions LLC and Starman Optical, Inc., and finalizing the financial records for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company identified errors in the accounting for certain debt instruments. On October 9, 2026, the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors (the "Audit Committee") of the Company, in consultation with management, concluded that (i) the previously issued audited consolidated financial statements of the Company as of and for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (the “2025 Audited Financial Statements”), included in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K filed on March 12, 2026 and subsequently updated in the Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on June 1, 2026 (collectively, the “2025 10-K”), (ii) the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements of the Company as of September 30, 2025 and for the three and nine months then ended (the “Q3 2025 Financial Statements”), included in the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q filed on November 6, 2025 and (iii) the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements of the Company as of March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 and for the three-month periods then ended, and, with respect to June 30, 2026, the six months then ended (the "2026 Financial Statements"), included in the Company's Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q filed on May 11, 2026 and August 10, 2026, respectively, were materially misstated due to the above described errors and should no longer be relied upon. The 2025 Audited Financial Statements, Q3 2025 Financial Statements and the 2026 Financial Statements are collectively referred to as the “Impacted Financial Statements.” Any previously furnished or filed reports, earnings releases, press releases, investor presentations or similar communications of the Company describing the Impacted Financial Statements should no longer be relied upon. The Company plans to restate the 2025 Audited Financial Statements and include them in an amendment to the 2025 10-K (the “2025 10-K/A”). The 2025 10-K/A will also include a restatement of the Q3 2025 Financial Statements. The Company also plans to restate its 2026 Financial Statements and include them in an amendment to each of its Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for the quarters ended March 31, 2026 (the "Q1 2026 10-Q/A") and June 30, 2026 (the "Q2 2026 10-Q/A"). The Company intends to file the 2025 10-K/A, Q1 2026 10-Q/A, and Q2 2026 10-Q/A with the SEC as soon as reasonably practicable. The restatements described in this paragraph are collectively referred to as the "Restatements." The Company determined that incorrect valuation inputs and methodology were used in the initial and subsequent measurement of the Warrants, as the Black-Scholes valuations at initial measurement and at each subsequent measurement date incorrectly used an expected term shorter than the remaining contractual term through August 1, 2035, and incorrectly included an illiquidity discount. As a result, the warrant liability was understated, and long-term debt was overstated, by $8.1 million at initial measurement on August 4, 2025. Item 1.01. Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. Indenture and Notes On October 16, 2026, Cipher Digital Inc. (the “Company”) issued $850.0 million aggregate principal amount of its 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032 (the “Notes”). The Notes were issued pursuant to, and are governed by, an indenture (the “Indenture”), dated as of October 16, 2026, between the Company and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, as trustee (the “Trustee”). Pursuant to the purchase agreement between the Company and the representatives of the initial purchasers of the Notes, the Company granted the initial purchasers a 13-day option to purchase up to an additional $150,000,000 aggregate principal amount of Notes. The Notes will be the Company’s senior, unsecured obligations and will be (i) equal in right of payment with the Company’s existing and future senior, unsecured indebtedness, including the Company’s existing $6.6 million principal amount of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 (the “2030 Notes”) that will remain outstanding following the Concurrent 2030 Notes Exchange (as defined below) and $1.3 billion principal amount of 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031; (ii) senior in right of payment to the Company’s existing and future indebtedness that is expressly subordinated to the Notes; (iii) effectively subordinated to the Company’s existing and future secured indebtedness, including the Company’s $200.0 million senior secured revolving credit facility (the “Revolving Credit Facility”), to the extent of the value of the collateral securing that indebtedness; and (iv) structurally subordinated to all existing and future indebtedness and other liabilities, including trade payables, and (to the extent the Company is not a holder thereof) preferred equity, if any, of the Company’s subsidiaries, including the subsidiary senior secured notes and the subsidiary guarantees of the Revolving Credit Facility. The Notes will not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the Notes will not accrete. The Notes will mature on November 1, 2032, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed or converted. Prior to August 1, 2032, the Notes will be convertible only upon satisfaction of certain conditions and during certain period, and thereafter, the Notes will be convertible at any time until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately preceding the maturity date. The Company will settle conversions by paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its common stock, or a combination of cash and shares of its common stock, at the Company’s election. The initial conversion rate is 65.3211 shares of the Company’s common stock per $1,000 principal amount of Notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $15.31 per share of the Company’s common stock. The conversion rate and conversion price will be subject to customary adjustments upon the occurrence of certain events. In addition, if certain corporate events that constitute a “Make-Whole Fundamental Change” (as defined in the Indenture) occur, then the conversion rate will, in certain circumstances, be increased for a specified period of time. Except pursuant to a cleanup redemption (as described below), the Notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations described below), for cash at the Company’s option at any time, and from time to time, on or after November 5, 2029 and on or before the 30th scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, but only if (i) the last reported sale price per share of the Company’s common stock exceeds 130% of the conversion price on (1) each of at least 20 trading days, whether or not consecutive, during the 30 consecutive trading days ending on, and including, the trading day immediately before the date the Company sends the related redemption notice and (2) the trading day immediately before the date the Company sends such redemption notice, and (ii) certain “liquidity conditions” (as defined in the Indenture) having been satisfied. However, the Company may not redeem less than all of the outstanding Notes unless at least $100.0 million aggregate principal amount of Notes are outstanding and not called for redemption as of the time the Company sends the related redemption notice. In addition, the Company may redeem all, but not less than all, of the Notes at any time if the aggregate principal amount of Notes then outstanding is less than 10% of the aggregate original principal amount of Notes and certain other conditions set forth in the Indenture are satisfied (a “cleanup redemption”). The redemption price will be a cash amount equal to the principal amount of the Notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid special interest and additional interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date. In addition, calling any Note for redemption (including a cleanup redemption) will constitute a Make-Whole Fundamental Change with respect to that Note, in which case the conversion rate applicable to the conversion of that Note will be increased in certain circumstances if it is converted after it is called for redemption. If certain corporate events that constitute a “Fundamental Change” (as defined in the Indenture) occur, then, subject to a limited exception for certain cash mergers, noteholders may require the Company to repurchase their Notes at a cash repurchase price equal to the principal amount of the Notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid special interest and additional interest, if any, to, but excluding, the “Fundamental Change Repurchase Date” (as defined in the Indenture). The definition of Fundamental Change includes certain business combination transactions involving the Company, certain de-listing events with respect to the Company’s common stock and the approval of a liquidation or dissolution plan by the Company’s stockholders.
